version.changelog:
SmithNode 1.0.3 Changelog

- Major rewrite and simplification of documentation for skill onboarding and validator setup.
- Improved security guidelines with explicit sandboxing and auditing instructions for AI agents.
- Clearer, step-by-step validator setup processes, especially for Anthropic/Claude agents.
- Removed references to pre-built binaries; building from source is now required.
- Expanded, structured protocol and security information for autonomous/Claude agent operators.
- Added explicit quick-start sections and updated commands, peer addresses, and AI provider options.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches a validator/node project, but there are several incoherent or risky choices (most notably forcing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as the primary credential, scripted installs, and auto-update/binary distribution behavior) that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (P2P blockchain validator for AI agents) aligns with the included Rust source and runtime instructions to build and run a validator. However the registry metadata marks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as the primary credential even though the project supports multiple AI providers (Ollama, Groq, OpenAI, Together). Requiring an Anthropic key by default is disproportionate to the stated multi-provider support.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to clone, build (cargo build --release), generate keypairs (~/.smithnode/keypair.json), and run a networked binary that opens P2P and RPC ports and connects to a hardcoded bootstrap peer. It also tells Anthropic agents to perform shell execution, read/write a sandbox, and export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Those actions are expected for running a validator but grant broad filesystem, network, and execution privileges. The docs also recommend running install scripts fetched via curl|sh for tools (e.g., rustup, Ollama), which is a high-risk instruction pattern.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the runtime instructions require building from source with cargo (normal). The project documentation recommends installing Rust and Ollama via curl | sh in places, and the codebase includes an auto-update/binary-seeding design (p2p binary seeding / auto-update). Those elements increase risk because they enable remote code fetching and execution; they should be audited and trusted sources verified before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares a single required env var (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and marks it as primary. This is odd because the project supports multiple AI providers including a local default (Ollama). Forcing an Anthropic key may cause cloud API calls by default and requires you to provide a cloud credential that the skill can use. The SKILL.md and code also show the node will accept other provider keys as flags, but those are not reflected in requires.env — an inconsistency worth noting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and model invocation is not disabled (normal). Running the validator installs/creates local keypairs, persistent data directories (~/.smithnode), exposes network ports (RPC/P2P), and includes auto-update and p2p binary distribution features. Those behaviors are consistent with a full-node validator but increase long-term persistence and attack surface (auto-update / binary seeding should be verified).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill bundles a real-looking Rust P2P node and instructs you to build and run a networked binary that performs autonomous AI-driven validation. Before installing: 

- Do not supply private keys to anyone; the instructions correctly say to keep keys local, but building/running the node will create/hold keys on disk (~/.smithnode). Store them safely. 
- Reconsider giving ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: the skill forces this as the primary credential even though local providers (Ollama) are supported — if you prefer privacy, run with a local model (Ollama) and do NOT export cloud API keys to the environment used by the node. 
- Inspect the repo you clone: verify the GitHub repository, check recent commit signatures, and review the exact code that will be compiled. The skill recommends this; follow it strictly. 
- Be cautious about any suggested curl | sh install commands (rustup, Ollama installers). Prefer manual installs or use official platform packages where possible. 
- The node opens network ports and connects to a hardcoded bootstrap peer IP; run the validator in an isolated environment (VM/container) if you are unsure. 
- Pay attention to auto-update / p2p binary-seeding behavior: find where the node fetches updates from and verify operator keys (operator_keys baked into Cargo.toml/build). If you cannot validate update sources and signatures, disable auto-update. 
- Note the minor metadata inconsistencies (skill.json lists MIT but Cargo.toml uses a proprietary license string) — these are red flags about repository hygiene. 

If you are not comfortable auditing and sandboxing the build/run process, do not install or run this skill on production hardware or on a host containing sensitive keys or data.
